title: Algebra
tagline: Equations, progressions, and the binomial — patterns, not brute force.

subsections.title: Linear Equations in Two Variables
subsections.trick: Compare a/p, b/q, c/r before touching algebra — the ratio pattern tells you instantly whether it's one line, no solution, or a unique solution, without solving anything.

subsections.title: Binomial Theorem
subsections.trick: The (r+1)th term formula is your entry point for every ‘find the coefficient of x^k’ question — set the exponent of x equal to k and solve for r first, then plug back in.

subsections.title: Quadratic Equations
subsections.trick: Almost every CAT quadratic question wants sum/product of roots, not the roots themselves — use −b/a and c/a directly and skip the quadratic formula entirely. For max/min of ax²+bx+c, the vertex x = −b/2a is also the average of the two roots.

subsections.title: Cubic & Higher Degree Equations
subsections.trick: The sign of each root-sum formula alternates: +, +, − for a cubic’s three symmetric sums. Remainder Theorem (plug in x=a) is almost always faster than long division for ‘is (x−a) a factor’ questions.

formulas.latex: (x-a) \text{ is a factor of } f(x) \iff f(a)=0

subsections.title: AP, GP & HP
subsections.trick: If a question mixes three numbers in AP, GP and HP, remember (GM)² = AM × HM — it often replaces two equations with one. For GP sums, check r<1 vs r>1 before picking the formula, and don’t forget the infinite-sum formula only applies for |r|<1.

subsections.title: Logarithms
subsections.trick: Change of base (formula 10) is the escape hatch whenever a log question mixes different bases — route everything through a common base and the rest collapses. Base 10 is the default unless stated otherwise.
